{{Quote|Rogue One? There is no Rogue One!|The dispatcher, while communicating with the Rogue One crew|audio=ThereIsNoRogueOne.flac|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
An '''individual''' worked as a base control dispatcher and served as an [[Alliance officer|officer]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]] as part of the [[Massassi Group]]. The staffer made contact with [[starship]]s leaving the rebel base at the [[Great Temple]] on Yavin.

In [[1 BBY]], the [[officer]] attempted to prevent the unauthorized departures of [[Captain]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor]]'s crew and later the team that became known as [[Rogue One]], both of which left to carry out critical missions, ignoring the officer's orders.

==Biography==
{{Quote|U-wing, Yavin Tower. You have not been authorized to leave the base. You need to stand down and return immediately.|The officer, hailing Cassian Andor's crew|audio=UwingYavinTower.flac|<ref name="WhoElseKnows">{{Andor|Who Else Knows?}}</ref>}}
Serving with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]'s [[Massassi Group]] at the [[Great Temple]] on<ref name="Rogue One" /> the [[moon]]<ref name="Novelization">[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]]</ref> [[Yavin 4]]<ref name="WhoElseKnows" /> by [[1 BBY]],<ref name="AndorDate">{{AndorDate|211}}</ref> the base control dispatcher was an [[Alliance officer|officer]]<ref name="Novelization" /> who maintained contact with [[starship]]s on the tarmac departing the installation.<ref name="WhoElseKnows" />

[[File:AndorK2DisobeyingOrders.png|thumb|left|250px|Andor orders K-2SO to silence the comms after the dispatcher contacted them]]
In 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="AndorDate" /> when Alliance [[Captain]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor]] received a [[distress signal]] from [[Axis network]] operative [[Kleya Marki]] on<ref name="WhoElseKnows" /> the planet<ref name="Novelization" /> [[Coruscant]], he, along with [[KX-series security droid]] [[K-2SO]] and fellow rebel [[Ruescott Melshi]] covertly boarded a [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wing starfighter]] under the guise of an evaluation flight. From [[Yavin Tower]], the dispatcher established communications with the crew and warned that they were unauthorized to leave the base and instructed them to deboard the starcraft. Under Andor's command, K-2SO silenced the ship's comms and the crew jumped into [[hyperspace]].<ref name="WhoElseKnows" />

[[File:Jyn_Erso_Cassian_Andor_disguises.jpg|thumb|250px|The Rogue One crew ignored the dispatcher's warning that they were not allowed to leave base.]]
Later that year,<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> Andor, along with [[Jyn Erso]], [[Bodhi Rook]], K-2SO, and other operatives who collectively became as the [[Rogue One]] crew, boarded an impounded [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|''Zeta''-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle]] known as ''[[SW-0608]]'' at the Yavin 4 base with the intention of stealing the [[Death Star plans]] on<ref name="Rogue One" /> the [[planet]]<ref name="Novelization" /> [[Scarif]], against the wishes of the [[Alliance High Command]].<ref name="Rogue One" /> When the dispatcher noticed the boarding, they hailed the crew through the ship's [[comm unit]] from the rebel base's comms center<ref name="JuniorNovel">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]''</ref> asking for an explanation and informing the Rogue One crew they were not allowed onboard. When the dispatcher asked for the crew's callsign, Rook improvised the name "Rogue One," to which the [[officer]] objected that there was no such designation. Rook simply replied they were pulling away, piloting the ship off base and onwards to Scarif.<ref name="Rogue One" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I did this really melodramatic dispatcher on the tarmac of Yavin. ''[...]'' I was told it was gonna be replaced ''[...]'' and I get to the mix and, 'No, we're leaving it. We like it.' ''[...]'' So then when we come back, we're trying to have consistency because we're walking into ''Rogue One''... 'You gotta do it again.'|Tony Gilroy, on his voice cameos|<ref name="ColbertInterview">{{YouTube|video=nGAWOF5TtnE|text=You Don't Have to Know Anything About "Star Wars" to Watch "Andor" - Tony Gilroy|channel=@ColbertLateShow|name=The Late Show with Stephen Colbert|date=2025-06-06}}</ref>|audio=}}
[[File:TonyGilroy-SWcom.jpg|thumb|Writer Tony Gilroy provided the voice for the dispatcher]]
The dispatcher made their first, voice-only appearance in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', as well as in its [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|adult]]<ref name="Novelization" /> and [[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel|junior novelizations]],<ref name="JuniorNovel" /> which released the same day as the film on [[December 16]], [[2016]].<ref name="SW.com">{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books|author=[[James Floyd|Floyd, James]]|date=2016-12-14}}</ref> The character was voiced by [[Tony Gilroy]], co-writer for ''Rogue One'', although he was not formally credited for the role.<ref name="cameo">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/star-wars-tv-shows/andor-creator-tony-gilroy-has-a-hidden-cameo-during-the-star-wars-shows-final-episodes|text=Andor creator Tony Gilroy has a hidden cameo during the Star Wars show's final episodes|author=Emily Garbutt|date=2025-05-17|work=GamesRadar|archivedate=20250617010533}}</ref>

The officer later appeared via voice again in "[[Who Else Knows?]]," the eleventh episode in the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] of the [[Disney+]] live-action series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'',<ref name="WhoElseKnows" /> which aired on [[May 13]], [[2025]],<ref name="Trailer News">{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-teaser-trailer-key-art-reveal|text=First ''Andor A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer and Poster Revealed}}</ref> ''Andor'' creator Tony Gilroy once more played the part in an uncredited capacity.<ref name="cameo" /> According to Gilroy, his part in ''Rogue One'' was recorded to feed lines to actors and was originally intended to be replaced later, but his brother and editor [[John Gilroy]] made the decision to keep Tony's performance in the final cut. Tony was later asked to reprise his role in ''Andor'' to maintain consistency.<ref name="ColbertInterview" />
